title: Good and bad bishops
line: A bishop blocked by its own pawns, and what to do with it.

steps.text: Black's pawns on d5 and e6 stand on light squares. The bishop on c8 runs on light squares too, and those pawns block it.
A bishop hemmed in by its own pawns is a bad bishop. Tap Black's bad bishop.

wrong.f8: That bishop runs on dark squares. Black's center pawns stand on light squares, so they do not block it.

steps.after: A bishop whose own pawns stand on the other color has open roads: a good bishop.

steps.text: One cure is to trade it. Black pushes a pawn to b6, brings the bishop out to a6, and trades it for White's good bishop.
Here Black has not pushed the pawn in front of its king yet. Bring the bishop out first, before the pawns close it in.
steps.hint: The bishop leaves along the diagonal toward your king's side of the board.
steps.after: The bishop is outside the pawn chain.

steps.text: Now push the pawn in front of your king one square. The bishop is already out, so it does not shut anything in.
steps.after: Black's pawns sit on light squares, but its light-squared bishop is free.

summary: A bishop blocked by its own pawns is a bad bishop. Get it out before the pawns close in, or trade it.
